div.font: This project began with a simple question: How can we distinguish between truth and falsehood?

font.span: Not "what do I prefer" or "what comforts me" or even "what affirms my beliefs", but identifying what is actually true -
font.b: by the same standards we use to distinguish truth anywhere else
font.span: . In practical terms, we want to figure out: "
font.b: given the abundance of information (where much of it false and only some of it true),

span.b: what conditions are required to reliably and confidently filter falsehood from truth

font.font: This project functions as that progressive filter, where each section adds a set of necessary conditions for truth to remain distinguishable from fabrication. When any of these necessary constraints are rejected, the original question collapses - because what remains can be used to justify both truth and falsehood, making them indistinguishable (thus allowing us to validly defend false beliefs, without realizing). What follows is the path that allows us to derive the natural conclusions from narrowing these hierarchical constraints.

switch.text: 3. Building Confidence [in Logical and Historical Claims]

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 301px; height: 1px; padding-top: 515px; margin-left: 23px;

div.font: - Claims (ie. information that are true or false) can't be justified by assuming itself - that is assertion, not justification or proof.
- Any approach that can be used to "prove" falsehood makes truth and falsehood indistinguishable.
- Logical confidence requires axioms grounded in reality, premises grounded in axioms, internal and external consistency, and absence of valid objections and alternative explanations.
- Historical confidence requires eyewitnesses and archaeology, independent corroboration, traceable and unbroken chains, and strong resistance to fabrication.

switch.text: - Claims (ie. information that are true or false) can't be justified by assuming itself - that is assertion, not justification or proof....
